source.paper: CBSE Sample Question Paper 2025-26, Social Science (087)

questions.question: 'Democracy leads to peaceful and harmonious life among citizens in every sphere.' Support this statement with suitable arguments.
answer_steps: Democracies accommodate various social divisions; for example, Belgium peacefully solved its ethnic problems. Democracies develop a procedure to conduct competition (elections, power sharing), which reduces the chance of tensions turning violent.
Democracy teaches people to respect differences and resolve conflicts among groups peacefully, while non-democratic rulers ignore or suppress differences, as in Sri Lanka.

Democracy is not just rule by majority opinion: the majority works with the minority, and rule by majority does not become rule by one religious, racial or linguistic community, so every citizen has a chance to be in the majority.

questions.question: How does democracy produce an accountable, responsive and legitimate government?
answer_steps: Accountable: people have the right to choose their rulers and control over them through regular, free and fair elections.
Open public debate on major policies and legislation, and citizens' right to information about the government, make the government answerable.
Transparency: citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision making, for example through the Right to Information Act, 2005.
Responsive: decisions are based on deliberation and negotiation, so they may be slower but more acceptable and effective; elected governments must respond to people's needs to win again.
Legitimate: even if it is slow or less efficient, a democratic government is people's own government, which is why support for democracy is overwhelming.

questions.question: What are the conditions under which democracies accommodate social diversities?
answer_steps: Democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion: the majority always needs to work with the minority so that the government represents the general view.
Rule by majority must not become rule by a majority community in terms of religion, race or linguistic group.
Every citizen must have a chance of being in the majority at some point of time; if anyone is barred from it on the basis of birth, democracy stops being accommodative.

questions.question: Give arguments to refute the assertion: 'Industrialised countries can afford democracy but the poor need dictatorship to become rich.'
answer_steps: Between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships grew only slightly faster than democracies, and among poor countries the difference (4.34% against 4.28%) is negligible.
Economic development depends on several factors such as population size, the global situation, cooperation from other countries and economic priorities, not on dictatorship.
Democracy also gives other benefits, such as accountable and legitimate government, dignity and freedom, so it is better to prefer democracy.

questions.question: Give arguments to support or refute the assertion: 'Democracy can't reduce inequality of incomes between different citizens.'
answer_steps: Support: democracies ensure political equality, but economic inequality is growing; the ultra-rich have an increasing share of income while the poor find it hard to meet basic needs.
Refute: the poor form a large share of voters, so they can use their votes to press governments for welfare and anti-poverty policies.
Conclusion: democracy does not reduce inequality by itself; it creates conditions that citizens must use to demand such policies.

questions.question: Give arguments to refute the assertion: 'In a democracy all citizens have one vote, which means that there is absence of any domination and conflict.'
answer_steps: One vote for every citizen ensures political equality, but it does not remove economic and social inequality.
Domination can continue through money and muscle power, caste and communal politics, or a fixed majority community.
Conflicts among groups still arise; democracy only provides peaceful ways to negotiate them, as Belgium did and Sri Lanka failed to do.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

*Nannu is a daily wage earner. He lives in Welcome Mazdoor Colony, a slum habitation in East Delhi. He lost his ration card and applied for a duplicate one. He made several rounds to the local Food and Civil Supplies office for the next three months. But the clerks and officials would not even look at him, leave alone do his job or bother to tell him the status of his application. Ultimately, he filed an application under the Right to Information Act asking for the daily progress made on his application, names of the officials who were supposed to act on his application and what action would be taken against these officials for their inaction. Within a week of filing the application under the Right to Information Act, he was visited by an inspector from the Food Department, who informed him that the card had been made and he could collect it from the office.* (NCERT)

(i) What does Nannu's example show about democracy? (1)

(ii) Which right did Nannu use? (1)

(iii) How does this right make the government accountable? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Ordinary citizens in a democracy can make the government work and respond to their needs.
(ii) The Right to Information (Right to Information Act, 2005).
(iii) It gives citizens the right and the means to examine the process of decision making and ask officials about delays, so officials know they can be questioned and act faster.

questions.question: Why may democratic decisions take more time but be more effective?
answer_steps: Democracy is based on deliberation and negotiation, so decisions take time.

questions.question: Why can we not say that democracy guarantees economic development?
answer_steps: Between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships had a slightly higher rate of growth than democracies.
Economic development depends on several factors such as population size, the global situation, cooperation from other countries and economic priorities.

questions.question: How has democracy helped women and disadvantaged castes?
answer_steps: Long struggles in democracies made respect and equal treatment of women accepted principles, so women can fight what is legally and morally unacceptable.
Democracy strengthened the claims of disadvantaged castes for equal status and opportunity; caste atrocities now lack moral and legal foundations.

questions.question: 'Democracies have not been very successful in reducing economic inequality.' Explain.
answer_steps: Democracies are based on political equality, giving every individual equal weight in electing representatives, but economic inequality is growing.
A small number of ultra-rich enjoy a highly disproportionate and increasing share of wealth and income, while those at the bottom find it hard to meet basic needs.
Though the poor form a large proportion of voters, elected governments are not as keen to address poverty as expected; in some countries like Bangladesh, more than half the people lived in poverty.

questions.question: 'Democracy is accountable but not always responsive.' Explain.
answer_steps: Democracies have mechanisms of accountability: regular, free and fair elections, open public debate and citizens' right to information.
But democracies often frustrate the needs of the people and ignore the demands of a majority of the population.
Corruption also remains, though there is no evidence that non-democracies are less corrupt; still, a democratic government is legitimate as it is people's own government.

questions.question: Why are complaints about democracy a testimony to its success?
answer_steps: As people get some benefits of democracy, they ask for more and want to make democracy better.
Complaints show that people have developed awareness and the ability to look critically at power holders.
Democracy has transformed people from subjects into citizens, and most believe their vote makes a difference.

questions.question: How does democracy accommodate social diversity? What conditions are necessary for it?
answer_steps: Democracies develop a procedure to conduct competition among groups, such as elections and power sharing, which reduces the chance of tensions becoming violent.
No society can fully resolve conflicts, but democracy teaches people to respect differences and evolves ways to negotiate them; Belgium is an example.
Non-democratic regimes ignore or suppress differences, so handling diversity is a plus point of democracy; Sri Lanka shows what happens when conditions are not met.
Condition 1: democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion; the majority must work with the minority so that the government represents the general view.
Condition 2: rule by majority must not become rule by a majority community of religion, race or language; every citizen must have a chance of being in the majority at some time.

questions.question: Assess democracy on the basis of its outcomes.
answer_steps: Government: democracy produces accountable and legitimate government through elections, open debate and the right to information, though it is not always responsive and corruption remains.
Economic growth: dictatorships grew slightly faster from 1950 to 2000, but the difference is negligible and growth depends on many factors.
Inequality and poverty: democracy ensures political equality, but economic inequality is growing and poverty remains a serious problem.
Social diversity: democracy handles social differences peacefully if the majority works with the minority and no community is a permanent majority.
Dignity and freedom: democracy is far superior in promoting the dignity of individuals, women and disadvantaged castes; overall it is better because it is people's own government.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"If you consider all democracies and all dictatorships for the fifty years between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships have slightly higher rate of economic growth. The inability of democracy to achieve higher economic development worries us. But this alone cannot be reason to reject democracy. Economic development depends on several factors."* (NCERT)

(i) Which regime had a slightly higher growth rate between 1950 and 2000? (1)

(ii) Name any two factors on which economic development depends. (1)

(iii) Why should we still prefer democracy? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Dictatorships.
(ii) Any two: population size; the global situation; cooperation from other countries; the economic priorities adopted by the country.

(iii) The difference in growth rates, especially among poor countries, is negligible, and democracy has several other positive outcomes such as accountable and legitimate government, dignity and freedom.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"Democracy stands much superior to any other form of government in promoting dignity and freedom of the individual. Every individual wants to receive respect from fellow beings. Often conflicts arise among individuals because some feel that they are not treated with due respect."* (NCERT)

(i) In which respect is democracy superior to other forms of government according to the source? (1)

(ii) Why do conflicts often arise among individuals? (1)

(iii) How has democracy helped women and disadvantaged castes? (2)
answer_steps: (i) In promoting the dignity and freedom of the individual.
(ii) Because some feel that they are not treated with due respect.

(iii) Respect and equal treatment of women became accepted principles, making it easier for women to struggle against injustice; democracy strengthened the claims of disadvantaged castes for equal status and opportunity, and caste atrocities lack moral and legal foundations.
